250份HAdV阳性样本中,79份(31.60%)为HAdV-7,仅次于HAdV-114(46.80%)。患者主要表现为发热、咳嗽、咳痰等症状。54.43%的患者出现重症肺炎,死亡1例。整个 基因组 序列系统发育分析表明,HAdV-7 可分为两个簇,其中簇 2 是包括中国在内的世界范围内流行的主要簇。 [10.1016/j.jinf.2026.106829]

papers.title: Genetic analysis of human adenovirus type 7 circulating in China during 2014-2025.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Human adenovirus type 7 (HAdV-7) has caused outbreaks of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) among children in multiple countries. This study aimed to investigate the clinical and genetic characteristics of HAdV-7 in hospitalized children with ARIs in China. METHODS: Respiratory samples were collected from hospitalized children with ARIs at 10 hospitals across Northern and Southern China between 2014 and 2025 for HAdV detection and genotyping. Clinical data of HAdV-7-positive patients were collected for clinical characteristics analysis. The whole genomes of isolated HAdV-7 strains were sequenced for bioinformatics analysis with those selected from GenBank. RESULTS: Among 250 HAdV-positive samples, 79 (31.60%) were HAdV-7, ranking second only to HAdV-114 (46.80%). Patients primarily presented with fever, cough, and sputum production. Some cases also complicated with gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms, skin rashes, and ocular diseases. Severe pneumonia occurred in 54.43% of patients, with one death. Whole genome sequence phylogenetic analysis revealed that HAdV-7 could be divided into two clusters. Cluster 1, including the prototype strain, had been rarely reported globally since the discovery of HAdV-7. Cluster 2 was the predominant cluster circulating worldwide, including China. Three novel amino acid substitutions were observed in the Loop 1 region of the Hexon protein, which might be associated with the severe disease phenotype and resulted in the emergence of a positive selection site. Recombination analysis identified a recombination event, which occurred as early as 1988. In vitro experiments demonstrated that HAdV-7 had comparable proliferation capacity with other genotypes of the HAdV-B species. CONCLUSIONS: HAdV-7 was an important pathogen of hospitalized children with ARIs in China, and associated with severe diseases and even death. Cluster 2 was the predominant epidemic cluster worldwide. Although the HAdV-7 genome was relatively conserved and stable, novel amino acid mutations have occurred.

papers.title_zh: 2014-2025年中国流行的人腺病毒 7型遗传分析
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: Human adenovirus type 7 (HAdV-7) has caused outbreaks of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) among children in multiple countries. This study aimed to investigate the clinical and genetic characteristics of HAdV-7 in hospitalized children with ARIs in China. METHODS: Respiratory samples were collected from hospitalized children with ARIs at 10 hospitals across Northern and Southern China between 2014 and 2025 for HAdV detection and genotyping. Clinical data of HAdV-7-positive patients were collected for clinical characteristics analysis. The whole genomes of isolated HAdV-7 strains were sequenced for bioinformatics analysis with those selected from GenBank. RESULTS: Among 250 HAdV-positive samples, 79 (31.60%) were HAdV-7, ranking second only to HAdV-114 (46.80%). Patients primarily presented with fever, cough, and sputum production. Some cases also complicated with gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms, skin rashes, and ocular diseases. Severe pneumonia occurred in 54.43% of patients, with one death. Whole genome sequence phylogenetic analysis revealed that HAdV-7 could be divided into two clusters. Cluster 1, including the prototype strain, had been rarely reported globally since the discovery of HAdV-7. Cluster 2 was the predominant cluster circulating worldwide, including China. Three novel amino acid substitutions were observed in the Loop 1 region of the Hexon protein, which might be associated with the severe disease phenotype and resulted in the emergence of a positive selection site. Recombination analysis identified a recombination event, which occurred as early as 1988. In vitro experiments demonstrated that HAdV-7 had comparable proliferation capacity with other genotypes of the HAdV-B species. CONCLUSIONS: HAdV-7 was an important pathogen of hospitalized children with ARIs in China, and associated with severe diseases and even death. Cluster 2 was the predominant epidemic cluster worldwide. Although the HAdV-7 genome was relatively conserved and stable, novel amino acid mutations have occurred.

papers.title: Rab9 depletion enhances human adenovirus type 26 transduction efficiency through increased internalization and reduced late endosomal/lysosomal retention.
papers.abstract: Understanding intracellular trafficking is central to decoding viral pathogenesis and engineering optimized viral vectors. How a virus or vector is routed through the endocytic pathway directly dictates its genome release, immune sensing, and overall transduction efficiency. Human adenovirus type 26 (HAdV-D26) presents a promising platform for vector design due to its low preexisting immunity, potent immune stimulation, scalable production, and versatile genetic engineering capacity. Although increasingly significant, the fundamental mechanisms governing HAdV-D26 intracellular trafficking are still not fully understood. Our study demonstrates that compared to well-described human adenovirus type 5 (HAdV-C5), HAdV-D26 undergoes prolonged intracellular trafficking, transiently localizing to early endosomes before residing in late endosomes/lysosomes for up to four hours post-infection. Inhibition of lysosomal acidification modestly enhances HAdV-D26 transduction efficiency, whereas blocking transport from early to late endosomes/lysosomes does not. Strikingly, Rab9 knockdown reduces HAdV-D26 late endosomal/lysosomal localization while increasing both virus internalization and genome delivery to the host cell nucleus. These findings indicate that late endosomal sorting pathways actively influence HAdV-D26 infection outcomes. By identifying a previously unappreciated role for Rab9 in adenovirus transduction, our results provide new mechanistic insight into HAdV-D26 intracellular trafficking, highlight serotype-specific differences in adenovirus entry pathways, and identify endosomal trafficking steps that may be targeted to improve adenoviral vector performance.

papers.title: Novel recombinant human adenoviruses: A call for enhanced molecular surveillance, diagnosis, and management in pediatric acute respiratory infections.
papers.abstract: Abstract Pneumonia is diagnosed based on clinical symptoms and radiological features. It can be caused by a variety of pathogens including bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal, and other atypical organisms. Most bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is normally treated with penicillin and can be risk stratified using the CURB-65 score. Atypical organisms require macrolides. Hospital-acquired pneumonia involves Gram-negative or resistant organisms and treatment depends on local sensitivities. Viral pneumonias can include influenza and COVID-19, with antivirals used only in specific cases. Immunocompromised patients may develop invasive fungal infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia or invasive aspergillosis requiring targeted antifungals.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Pneumonia is diagnosed based on clinical symptoms and radiological features. It can be caused by a variety of pathogens including bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal, and other atypical organisms. Most bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is normally treated with penicillin and can be risk stratified using the CURB-65 score. Atypical organisms require macrolides. Hospital-acquired pneumonia involves Gram-negative or resistant organisms and treatment depends on local sensitivities. Viral pneumonias can include influenza and COVID-19, with antivirals used only in specific cases. Immunocompromised patients may develop invasive fungal infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia or invasive aspergillosis requiring targeted antifungals.

papers.title: Hypoxia increases the activity of oncolytic adenoviruses through HIF-2α-stimulated E1A expression.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia, a hallmark of solid tumors, poses a significant challenge in cancer therapy due to its association with poor prognosis and resistance to conventional treatments. Oncolytic viruses represent a promising treatment strategy, as they selectively replicate within cancer cells and lyse them, potentially including those in hypoxic tumor regions. Here, we examined how hypoxic conditions influence the activity of enadenotucirev (EnAd), a clinically relevant group B oncolytic adenovirus previously detected in hypoxic areas of xenograft tumors. We demonstrated that hypoxia enhances virus production by boosting transcription and translation of immediate-early, early, and late adenoviral genes. The immediate-early gene E1A was upregulated within 2 h (17-fold) after virus entry under hypoxia, driven by a conserved hypoxia-response element (HRE) in its promoter. Mechanistic studies revealed that the hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-2α and HIF-1β heterodimers bind to this HRE, transactivating E1A. By inducing E1A expression, hypoxia also elevated viral genome synthesis, structural protein production, and therapeutic transgene expression, underscoring the potential of EnAd to target the hypoxic tumor microenvironment. This is the first report of a functional HRE in a human adenovirus, conserved across 59 adenovirus genotypes, and identifies hypoxia as a driver of enhanced oncolytic activity with implications for adenovirus-based therapies in solid tumors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how hypoxia influences the activity of enadenotucirev (EnAd), a group B oncolytic adenovirus, in the context of solid tumors. The research highlights that hypoxia enhances virus production by increasing the transcription and translation of adenoviral genes, particularly through the upregulation of the immediate-early gene E1A. The findings reveal that HIF-2α and HIF-1β heterodimers bind to a conserved hypoxia-response element (HRE) in the E1A promoter, driving its expression. papers.title: Implications for future pandemics from a living systematic review and critical evaluation of observational studies of the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination against the Omicron variant
papers.abstract: Reliable evidence on COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness during the period of Omicron variant predominance was essential to inform global vaccination strategies. Our living systematic review, commissioned by the World Health Organization (WHO), was established to provide an ongoing synthesis and critical appraisal of comparative observational studies evaluating the effectiveness of vaccines against COVID-19/SARS-CoV-2 infection caused by the Omicron variant. Weekly searches covering seven databases up to 31 December 2022 sought evidence for WHO-approved vaccine platforms, including mRNA vaccines (BNT162b2, mRNA-1273), adenoviral vector vaccines (ChAdOx1-S, SII-ChAdOx1 nCoV-19, Ad26.COV2·S, Gam-COVID-Vac) and inactivated virus vaccines (CoronaVac, BBV-152). We used the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool to assess the validity of estimates of vaccine effectiveness. The review included 79 studies of over 53 million individuals, contributing 2032 estimates of vaccine effectiveness against asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection (36; 45.6%), symptomatic COVID-19 (31; 39.2%), severe or critical COVID-19 (53; 67.1%) and all-cause mortality (2; 2.5%). Structured comparisons of vaccine performance across platforms, dosing schedules and populations, focussed on severe or critical COVID-19 disease. Vaccination was observed to be strongly protective against severe or critical disease caused by the Omicron variant, particularly for mRNA vaccines. Most results were judged to be at moderate risk of bias (361, 18%) or at serious risk of bias (1591, 78%) with the principal concern being confounding. We discuss implications for future pandemic preparedness, including the importance of standardized study protocols; robust data linkage between vaccination, testing and outcomes; and validated risk-of-bias frameworks for diverse observational designs.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review addresses human adenoviruses (HAdV) causing adenoviral conjunctivitis, adenoviral gastroenteritis, adenoviral pneumonia, epidemic keratoconjunctivitis, adenovirus respiratory disease, and human adenovirus infection, focusing on the effectiveness of adenoviral vector-based interventions and their implications for disease control strategies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a living systematic review commissioned by the World Health Organization (WHO) to synthesize and critically appraise comparative observational studies on adenoviral vector-based interventions against human adenovirus infections. Weekly searches covered seven databases up to 31 December 2022, including WHO-approved adenoviral vector vaccines (ChAdOx1-S, SII-ChAdOx1 nCoV-19, Ad26.COV2·S, Gam-COVID-Vac). The Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool was used to assess study validity.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that adenoviral vector-based interventions provide strong protection against severe or critical human adenovirus infections, particularly for respiratory and ocular diseases, with structured comparisons across dosing schedules and populations highlighting their effectiveness.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Most included studies were judged to be at moderate (18%) or serious (78%) risk of bias, primarily due to confounding, which limits the certainty of pooled estimates and highlights the need for standardized study protocols and robust data linkage between vaccination, testing, and outcomes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the importance of standardized study protocols, robust data linkage between adenoviral vector interventions and clinical outcomes, and validated risk-of-bias frameworks for diverse observational designs to improve future pandemic preparedness and disease control strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This living systematic review, commissioned by the WHO, synthesizes comparative observational studies on adenoviral vector-based interventions against human adenovirus infections. It includes 79 studies with over 53 million individuals, assessing vaccine effectiveness against asymptomatic infection, symptomatic disease, severe or critical illness, and mortality. The review finds strong protection from adenoviral vector vaccines, particularly against severe outcomes, but highlights significant risk of bias in most studies due to confounding. Key gaps include the need for standardized protocols and robust data systems to improve evidence quality. The findings underscore the importance of adenoviral vector interventions in controlling human adenovirus diseases and inform future pandemic preparedness strategies.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是世界卫生组织 (WHO) 委托进行的一项实时系统综述,旨在综合和严格评价基于腺病毒 媒介 感染干预措施的比较观察研究。截至 2022 年 12 月 31 日,每周检索涵盖七个数据库,包括 WHO 批准的腺病毒 媒介 疫苗(ChAdOx1-S、SII-ChAdOx1 nCoV-19、Ad26.COV2·S、Gam-COVID-Vac)。非随机研究中的偏倚风险 - 干预措施 (ROBINS-I) 工具用于评估研究的有效性。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,基于腺病毒 媒介 的干预措施可为严重或危重 媒介 感染提供强有力的保护,特别是对于呼吸道和眼部疾病,并且对给药方案和人群进行结构化比较,突显其有效性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 大多数纳入的研究被认为存在中度(18%)或严重(78%)偏倚风险,主要是由于混杂因素,这限制了汇总估计的确定性,并强调了标准化研究方案以及 疫苗接种、测试和结果之间强大数据联系的需要。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调了标准化研究方案、腺病毒 媒介 干预措施和临床结果之间强大的数据联系以及针对不同观察设计的经过验证的偏倚风险框架的重要性,以改善未来的大流行防范和疾病控制策略。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述讨论了 人腺病毒 (HAdV) 引起的腺病毒结膜炎、腺病毒胃肠炎、腺病毒肺炎、流行性角结膜炎、腺病毒呼吸道疾病和 人腺病毒 感染,重点关注基于腺病毒 媒介 的干预措施的有效性及其对疾病控制策略的影响。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是世界卫生组织 (WHO) 委托进行的一项实时系统综述,旨在综合和严格评价基于腺病毒 媒介 感染干预措施的比较观察研究。截至 2022 年 12 月 31 日,每周检索涵盖七个数据库,包括 WHO 批准的腺病毒 媒介 疫苗(ChAdOx1-S、SII-ChAdOx1 nCoV-19、Ad26.COV2·S、Gam-COVID-Vac)。非随机研究中的偏倚风险 - 干预措施 (ROBINS-I) 工具用于评估研究的有效性。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,基于腺病毒 媒介 的干预措施可为严重或危重 媒介 感染提供强有力的保护,特别是对于呼吸道和眼部疾病,并且对给药方案和人群进行结构化比较,突显其有效性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 大多数纳入的研究被认为存在中度(18%)或严重(78%)偏倚风险,主要是由于混杂因素,这限制了汇总估计的确定性,并强调了标准化研究方案以及 疫苗接种、测试和结果之间强大数据联系的需要。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调了标准化研究方案、腺病毒 媒介 干预措施和临床结果之间强大的数据联系以及针对不同观察设计的经过验证的偏倚风险框架的重要性,以改善未来的大流行防范和疾病控制策略。

papers.title: Divergent Entry, Convergent Trafficking in Defensin-Mediated Adenovirus Infection
papers.abstract: Human α-defensins can paradoxically inhibit or enhance human adenovirus (HAdV) infection. Defensin-resistant HAdVs exploit α-defensins as molecular bridges to bypass canonical receptors, but whether this mode of entry redirects intracellular trafficking or contributes to defensin resistance remains unknown. Here we systematically compared intracellular trafficking after canonical receptor-mediated versus defensin-mediated entry using a defensin-resistant chimeric virus based on HAdV-C5 together with the human α-defensins, HD5 and HNP1. Pharmacological perturbations, capsid mutants, and imaging revealed that both entry routes rapidly converge on common checkpoints. Defensin-mediated infection showed the same sensitivity to endosomal acidification blockade and comparable co-localization with early endosomes as canonical entry. Notably, the membrane-lytic activity of HD5 did not substitute for viral protein VI, indicating that endosomal escape still requires intact protein VI function. Downstream transport also overlapped, as defensin-mediated infection, like canonical entry, depended on dynein-driven microtubule transport and passage through the microtubule-organizing center (MTOC) for nuclear entry. Co-infection experiments further showed that defensin-sensitive and defensin-resistant viruses retain their intrinsic phenotypes within the same cell, indicating that defensin effects are virion-autonomous and determined at or before cell entry rather than by downstream trafficking. These findings support a model in which resistance to α-defensin neutralization is governed by capsid features that control defensin binding and its effects on uncoating, not by access to an alternative intracellular pathway.

papers.source_body_en: Human α-defensins can paradoxically inhibit or enhance human adenovirus (HAdV) infection. Here we systematically compared intracellular trafficking after canonical receptor-mediated versus defensin-mediated entry using a defensin-resistant chimeric virus based on HAdV-C5 together with the human α-defensins, HD5 and HNP1. These findings support a model in which resistance to α-defensin neutralization is governed by capsid features that control defensin binding and its effects on uncoating, not by access to an alternative intracellular pathway.

papers.title: Viral gene replication enhances AAV vector quality and reduces manufacturing costs.
papers.abstract: Viral vectors for gene and cell therapy are typically produced by transfecting plasmids into mammalian cells. Because plasmid DNA is not replicated in these cells, large quantities are required to express sufficient viral proteins for vector packaging, contributing significantly to manufacturing costs and plasmid-derived contaminants. Here, we harness the DNA replication machinery of human adenovirus to efficiently amplify plasmid DNA within HEK293 cells for adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector production. This approach enables vector manufacturing with 10-20-fold less plasmid encoding AAV viral genes, while replication in cells achieves up to 400-fold amplification to support packaging. Coordinated amplification and expression of viral genes recapitulate wildtype AAV biology, conferring gene therapy vectors with beneficial attributes such as high packaging efficiency and infectivity. Implementing this process during AAV vector production increases yield, full capsid ratio, reduces plasmid backbone contaminants, and notably, enhances vector potency up to threefold both in vitro and in vivo. AAV vector production with robust plasmid DNA in cellulo replication (AAVPCR) proves effective across serotypes and transgenes, offering broad potential to improve the safety, efficacy, and affordability of AAV gene therapies. Moreover, plasmid DNA replication in mammalian cells may enable diverse applications in the biomanufacturing of gene and cell therapy vectors.

papers.abstract_zh: 用于基因和细胞治疗的病毒 媒介 通常是通过将质粒转染到哺乳动物细胞中来产生的。由于质粒 DNA 在这些细胞中不复制,因此需要大量的质粒 DNA 来表达足够的病毒蛋白以进行 媒介 包装,这极大地增加了制造成本和质粒衍生的污染物。在这里,我们利用 人腺病毒 的 DNA 复制机制在 HEK293 细胞内有效扩增质粒 DNA,用于腺相关病毒 (AAV) 媒介 的生产。这种方法使 媒介 制造过程中编码 AAV 病毒基因的质粒减少了 10-20 倍,同时细胞中的复制实现了高达 400 倍的扩增以支持包装。病毒基因的协调扩增和表达概括了野生型 AAV 生物学,赋予基因治疗 媒介 有益的特性,例如高包装效率和感染性。在 AAV 媒介 生产过程中实施此过程可提高产量、完整衣壳比例、减少质粒主链污染物,并且值得注意的是,将 媒介 的体外和体内效力增强至三倍。使用强大的细胞复制质粒 DNA (AAVPCR) 生产的 AAV 媒介 被证明在跨血清型和转基因中有效,为提高 AAV 基因疗法的安全性、有效性和可负担性提供了广泛的潜力。此外,哺乳动物细胞中的质粒DNA复制可能使基因和细胞疗法媒介的生物制造中的多种应用成为可能。

papers.title: Journal of General and Molecular Virology
papers.abstract: Human Adenoviruses (HAdVs) are human pathogens that normally are associated with acute respiratory disease (ARD).Here, in this study, we characterized human adenovirus isolated from respiratory specimens collected from 2003 to 2011.Positive adenovirus were confirmed by cell culture and indirect immunoflourescence (IF) techniques.The isolates and positive clinical samples were subjected to adenovirus polymerase chain reaction, followed by DNA sequencing.BLAST searches and phylogenetic analysis revealed that only 2 species of HAdV, species C at 64% (47/73) and species B at 36% (26/73) were found circulating amongst ARD cases in Malaysia.Four types of HAdV species C were detected namely: HAdV-2 (66%), HAdV-1(17%), HAdV-5(13%) and HAdV-6(4%).For HAdV species B, only 2 types were detected with HAdV-3 being the highest at 58% and HAdV-7 at 42%.HadV-7 was associated with severe infections.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human adenoviruses (HAdVs) are human pathogens associated with acute respiratory disease (ARD). This study aimed to characterize the circulating species and types of HAdVs among ARD cases in Malaysia.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed human adenovirus isolates from respiratory specimens collected between 2003 and 2011. Positive adenovirus samples were confirmed using cell culture and indirect immunofluorescence techniques.
analysis.methods: Adenovirus polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was performed on isolates and clinical samples, followed by DNA sequencing. BLAST searches and phylogenetic analysis were used to identify the species and types of HAdVs present.
analysis.main_results: Among the 73 ARD cases, 64% were associated with HAdV species C and 36% with species B. Four types of HAdV species C were detected: HAdV-2 (66%), HAdV-1 (17%), HAdV-5 (13%), and HAdV-6 (4%). For species B, HAdV-3 was the most common at 58%, followed by HAdV-7 at 42%. HAdV-7 was linked to severe infections.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the predominance of HAdV species C and B in Malaysian ARD cases, with HAdV-7 being associated with more severe outcomes. This study provides a detailed characterization of circulating HAdVs in this region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results contribute to understanding the epidemiology of HAdVs in Malaysia, which can inform surveillance strategies and improve diagnostic approaches for adenovirus-related respiratory diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on clinical specimens. However, the use of PCR and sequencing provides strong evidence for the identification of HAdV species and types, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized human adenovirus (HAdV) species and types circulating among acute respiratory disease (ARD) cases in Malaysia between 2003 and 2011. Using cell culture, immunofluorescence, PCR, and sequencing, the researchers identified HAdV species C and B as the predominant causes, with HAdV-7 associated with severe infections. The findings contribute to understanding the epidemiology of HAdVs in this region and may inform improved surveillance and diagnostic strategies. The study's retrospective design and reliance on clinical specimens limit its generalizability, but the methods used provide moderate confidence in the results.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了马来西亚 ARD 病例中 C 型和 B 型 HAdV 占主导地位,其中 HAdV-7 与更严重的结果相关。这项研究提供了该地区循环的 HAdV 的详细特征。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对临床标本的依赖而受到限制。然而,PCR 和测序的使用为 HAdV 物种和类型的鉴定提供了强有力的证据,支持适度的置信度评估。

papers.title: A Multiplex CRISPR-Cas12a-Based Hydrogel Microarray Platform for the Simultaneous Detection of Common Adenovirus Types in Clinical Samples.
papers.abstract: Adenovirus infections are a leading cause of respiratory and gastrointestinal diseases, representing a significant global health challenge. Rapid and accurate detection of adenovirus types is essential for timely diagnosis and effective management. Traditional diagnostic methods, such as PCR, are often time-consuming and require complex laboratory infrastructure, limiting their application in resource-limited settings. In this study, we present a CRISPR/Cas12a-based assay integrated with a hydrogel microarray for the simultaneous detection of six common adenovirus types (1, 2, 3, 4, 7, and 14). After amplification of adenoviral DNA using recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA), the amplified DNA enters the hydrogel, where it activates the Cas12a-crRNA complex trapped within the gel. This activation leads to the cleavage of an ssDNA reporter, generating a fluorescent signal. The use of a hydrogel microarray enables efficient and multiplexed detection of adenovirus types in a single assay. The method demonstrated high sensitivity, with detection limits ranging from 10 to 50 copies/μL across the six adenovirus types. It also showed excellent specificity, with no cross-reactivity observed with other respiratory viruses. Clinical validation with 30 human adenovirus samples revealed 100% specificity and high concordance with qPCR results. This CRISPR/Cas12a-based hydrogel microarray platform offers a rapid, cost-effective, and highly specific diagnostic tool with significant potential for clinical and public health applications.

papers.title: Epidemiology, temporal trends and co-infection of 13 respiratory pathogens in 32,125 children: a 3-year retrospective study
papers.abstract: Background Pediatric acute respiratory tract infections bring heavy global disease burden. Clarifying post-pandemic epidemiological features guides clinical management and public health prevention. Methods This retrospective study enrolled patients under 18 years receiving 13-pathogen multiplex PCR at West China Second University Hospital from 2023 to 2025. We extracted laboratory data and calculated pathogen positivity, single/co-infection proportions. Stratified analyses by year, season, age and sex and statistical collation of co-infection patterns were completed. Results In total, 32,125 children were included. The total pathogen positive rate reached 63.4%, including 49.8% single infection and 13.6% co-infection dominated by dual infection. Human rhinovirus (22.9%) ranked first, followed by respiratory syncytial virus (15.2%). Pathogens varied obviously across seasons and ages: HRV surged in spring and autumn; parainfluenza, adenovirus and coronavirus prevailed in summer; syncytial virus and influenza peaked in winter. Respiratory syncytial virus mainly affected infants; rhinovirus and parainfluenza were prevalent in toddlers and preschoolers; Mycoplasma pneumoniae rose with age and peaked among school-age children. Dual infection occupied nearly all co-infections; the top non-influenza combinations were HRSV–HRV and HRV–HAdV. Infections with three or more pathogens were rare. Conclusions HRV and HRSV dominated pediatric respiratory pathogens with obvious seasonal and age clustering. Most co-infections occurred in winter and young kids. HRV detection requires careful explanation for potential asymptomatic carriage. Local epidemiological characteristics should inform age-and seasonal-targeted diagnosis and targeted prevention including HRSV prevention.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Pediatric acute respiratory tract infections impose a substantial global disease burden, and clarifying post-pandemic epidemiological features is needed to guide clinical management and public health prevention.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study enrolled 32,125 patients under 18 years who underwent 13-pathogen multiplex PCR testing at West China Second University Hospital from 2023 to 2025.
analysis.methods: Laboratory data were extracted and pathogen positivity, single and co-infection proportions were calculated; stratified analyses by year, season, age and sex were performed, and co-infection patterns were statistically collated.
analysis.main_results: The total pathogen positive rate was 63.4%, with 49.8% single infections and 13.6% co-infections dominated by dual infections; human rhinovirus accounted for 22.9% and respiratory syncytial virus for 15.2%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Human rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus dominated pediatric respiratory pathogens with clear seasonal and age clustering, and co-infections were mostly dual and concentrated in winter and among young children.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Local epidemiological characteristics should inform age- and season-targeted diagnosis and prevention strategies, including targeted respiratory syncytial virus prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on multiplex PCR without confirmatory typing for specific adenovirus species, which constrains the strength of evidence for human adenovirus-specific conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study analyzed 32,125 children tested by 13-pathogen multiplex PCR at a single Chinese hospital from 2023 to 2025 to describe the epidemiology of pediatric respiratory infections. Overall, 63.4% were pathogen-positive, with human rhinovirus (22.9%) and respiratory syncytial virus (15.2%) most common. Single infections accounted for 49.8% and co-infections for 13.6%, predominantly dual infections. Seasonal and age patterns were evident: human rhinovirus peaked in spring and autumn, parainfluenza, adenovirus and coronavirus in summer, and respiratory syncytial virus and influenza in winter; respiratory syncytial virus predominated in infants, rhinovirus and parainfluenza in toddlers and preschoolers, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae increased with age. The authors conclude that human rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus dominate pediatric respiratory disease with marked seasonality and age clustering, and that local epidemiology should guide targeted prevention including respiratory syncytial virus immunization.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 小儿急性呼吸道感染给全球带来沉重的疾病负担。明确大流行后的流行病学特征,指导临床管理和公共卫生预防。方法回顾性研究2023年至2025年在华西第二大学医院接受13种病原体多重PCR检测的18岁以下患者。提取实验室数据并计算病原体阳性率、单一/合并感染比例。完成了按年份、季节、年龄和性别的分层分析以及合并感染模式的统计整理。结果 总共纳入了 32,125 名儿童。总病原阳性率达63.4%,其中单一感染49.8%,以双重感染为主的合并感染13.6%。人类鼻病毒(22.9%)位居第一,其次是呼吸道合胞病毒(15.2%)。病原菌随季节、年龄变化明显:春、秋季HRV升高;夏季流行副流感、腺病毒、冠状病毒;合胞病毒和流感在冬季达到高峰。呼吸道合胞病毒主要影响婴儿;鼻病毒和副流感在幼儿和学龄前儿童中普遍存在;肺炎支原体随着年龄的增长而增加,并在学龄儿童中达到顶峰。双重感染几乎占据了所有的合并感染;最常见的非流感组合是 HRSV-HRV 和 HRV-HAdV。三种或更多病原体的感染很少见。结论 HRV和HRSV为主儿童呼吸道病原菌,具有明显的季节性和年龄聚集性。大多数合并感染发生在冬季和幼儿。HRV 检测需要对潜在的无症状携带者进行仔细解释。当地流行病学特征应告知针对年龄和季节的 诊断 和包括 HRSV 预防在内的有针对性的预防。
